description: RouteRL is a Python environment for studying route choices by human drivers and autonomous vehicles. The COeXISTENCE group at Jagiellonian University combines SUMO microscopic traffic simulation with discrete-choice models for humans and multi-agent reinforcement learning for automated vehicles. Its TrafficEnvironment implements the PettingZoo AEC interface and supports learning libraries such as TorchRL. Users configure a road network, driver population and learning objectives, then collect experience and plot simulation results. Daily route-choice experiments can represent different network sizes; the package has no fixed geographic coverage, observation period or universal temporal resolution. Source, tutorials and installation instructions are public and free under MIT. SUMO must be installed separately for local use. A Code Ocean demonstration is optional and requires an account there, but that restriction does not apply to accessing the GitHub source. Learned policies depend on the supplied objectives, human-behaviour assumptions and training setup; the README does not establish field performance in a particular city. The tool supports traffic assignment and human-AI transport experiments using SUMO (model-sumo). Its published software article and archived release identify the reusable implementation.
